tolleson.title: City History
tolleson.introduction: Tolleson's history reflects its development from an agricultural settlement into a West Valley city with industrial, distribution, and residential communities.

events.title: The Tolleson family arrives in Arizona
events.summary: The Tolleson family migrated from South Carolina to Arizona in 1908.

events.title: The Tolleson family purchases a ranch
events.summary: The Tolleson family purchased a 160-acre ranch at the intersection of 91st Avenue and Van Buren Street for $16,000.

events.title: Tolleson is founded
events.summary: Walter G. and Alethea H. Tolleson founded Tolleson in 1912. The city's history identifies the reopened Ten Mile Store as the nucleus of the new town.

events.title: Tolleson incorporates
events.summary: Tolleson incorporated in 1929.

events.title: The Great Depression affects Tolleson
events.summary: Tolleson experienced the effects of the Great Depression during the 1930s.

events.title: The Census counts 910 residents
events.summary: The U.S. Census Bureau reports 910 residents in Tolleson in 1930. The figure appears in the 1940 Census of Population, Volume I, Arizona section, printed page 91, Table 5.

events.title: Agricultural production recovers
events.summary: Agriculture in the surrounding area began a recovery in the 1940s, providing an economic boost to Tolleson.

events.title: The Census counts 1,731 residents
events.summary: The U.S. Census Bureau reports 1,731 residents in Tolleson in 1940. The figure appears in the 1940 Census of Population, Volume I, Arizona section, printed page 91, Table 5.

events.title: The Census counts 3,042 residents
events.summary: The U.S. Census Bureau reports 3,042 residents in Tolleson in 1950. The figure appears in the 1960 Census of Population, Arizona section, printed page 4-9, Table 8.

events.title: Tolleson becomes known for vegetable production
events.summary: By the 1950s, Tolleson had become known as the 'Vegetable Center of the World.'

events.title: Agricultural employment declines
events.summary: The city's history describes a rapid decline in agribusiness during the early 1960s. Changes in farming machinery, shipping methods, and vegetable acreage reduced the need for packing sheds and associated employment.

events.title: The Census counts 3,886 residents
events.summary: The U.S. Census Bureau reports 3,886 residents in Tolleson in 1960. The figure appears in the 1960 Census of Population, Arizona section, printed page 4-9, Table 8.

events.title: Infrastructure investments support development
events.summary: During the 1970s, city planners developed a master plan, began street beautification projects, encouraged housing development, and built a $2 million sewage treatment plant to support industrial and residential growth.

events.title: The Census counts 3,881 residents
events.summary: The U.S. Census Bureau reports 3,881 residents in Tolleson in 1970. The figure appears in the 1980 Census of Population and Housing, Arizona, Table 2, Tolleson city row.

events.title: Distribution centers reshape the local economy
events.summary: Fry's Food and Drug and Albertson's distribution centers arrived during the 1980s. The city's history describes their role in attracting additional industrial development.

events.title: The Census counts 4,433 residents
events.summary: The U.S. Census Bureau reports 4,433 residents in Tolleson in 1980. The figure appears in the 1980 Census of Population and Housing, Arizona, Table 2, Tolleson city row.

events.title: The Census counts 4,434 residents
events.summary: The Tolleson Community Profile reports 4,434 residents in 1990. Its population table attributes the figures to the U.S. Bureau of the Census, March 2001.

events.title: The Census counts 4,974 residents
events.summary: The Tolleson Community Profile reports 4,974 residents in 2000. Its population table attributes the figures to the U.S. Bureau of the Census, March 2001.

events.title: The Census counts 6,545 residents
events.summary: The 2010 Census counted 6,545 residents in Tolleson on April 1, 2010.

events.title: The Census counts 7,216 residents
events.summary: The 2020 Census counted 7,216 residents in Tolleson on April 1, 2020.

events.title: The Census Bureau estimates Tolleson's population
events.summary: The U.S. Census Bureau estimated Tolleson's population at 9,224 as of July 1, 2025 (V2025). This is an estimate, not a decennial Census count.

avondale.title: Avondale History
avondale.introduction: Explore major chapters in Avondale's history, from the area's deeper Indigenous history and early settlement through incorporation, growth and the modern city. Expand the timeline to view the full researched chronology.

chapters.title: Indigenous history predates the modern city
chapters.summary: Long before Coldwater or the incorporated City of Avondale, O'odham and Piipaash peoples lived throughout and maintained deep relationships with the Salt and Gila river region. Their history and presence form part of the deeper history of the area that became Avondale.

chapters.title: Monument Hill anchors Arizona's land-surveying history
chapters.summary: Survey work at Monument Hill in 1851 and 1867 helped establish a reference point for the land-surveying system used across much of Arizona. Its historical importance was formally recognized when the site was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2002.

chapters.title: From Coldwater to Avondale
chapters.summary: Agricultural settlement, Billy Moore's Coldwater community, stage-stop businesses and a changing postal history all contributed to the development of the community that became Avondale. By 1911, City historical material describes the later town site taking shape with a new post office and the Avondale name.
chapters.dispute_note: Historical sources differ on part of the early Coldwater chronology. City histories associate Billy Moore and Coldwater with 1880, while Arizona Memory Project material citing Arizona Place Names gives 1897 for establishment of Coldwater. The dates may describe different milestones.

chapters.title: Agriculture and migration shape the community
chapters.summary: Agriculture deeply shaped Avondale's early economy and community life. Agricultural families and migrant workers, transportation improvements, schools, New Deal-era projects and federal migrant housing all became part of the developing community during the first half of the twentieth century.

chapters.title: Avondale becomes an incorporated community
chapters.summary: Avondale incorporated on December 16, 1946. Municipal police and fire services followed, and the postwar years brought continued development of local institutions, schools and community traditions.

chapters.title: Phoenix Raceway becomes an Avondale landmark
chapters.summary: Phoenix International Raceway opened in Avondale in 1964 and grew into one of the city's most recognizable landmarks. In 1988, the facility hosted its first NASCAR Cup Series race.

chapters.title: Avondale grows into a major West Valley city
chapters.summary: Avondale grew from 6,151 residents in 1960 to 89,334 in the 2020 Census. The fastest expansion came during the late twentieth and early twenty-first centuries, transforming the scale of the city while residents continued preserving its community history.

chapters.title: Avondale marks 80 years since incorporation
chapters.summary: In 2026, Avondale marked eight decades since its December 1946 incorporation, connecting today's city with generations of residents who shaped the community.

events.title: Indigenous history predates the modern city
events.summary: Long before Coldwater or the incorporated City of Avondale, O'odham and Piipaash peoples lived throughout and maintained deep relationships with the Salt and Gila river region. Tribal histories connect their ancestors with the Phoenix Valley and lower Gila River and describe continued O'odham and Piipaash presence into the present.

events.title: Boundary survey establishes a monument at Monument Hill
events.summary: A monument was established at Monument Hill during federal boundary-survey work following the Mexican-American War and the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo.

events.title: Monument Hill becomes central to Arizona land surveying
events.summary: Monument Hill became associated with the Initial Point of the Gila and Salt River Base Line and Meridian, the surveying framework used for extensive federal land surveys in Arizona.

events.title: Federal land policy encourages agricultural settlement
events.summary: City historical material identifies the Desert Land Act of 1877 as part of the context that encouraged agricultural settlement in the area.

events.title: Billy Moore settles near the Agua Fria River
events.summary: City of Avondale histories place William G. "Billy" Moore near the Agua Fria River in 1880 and associate his settlement with the name Coldwater. Arizona Memory Project material citing Arizona Place Names instead dates the establishment of Coldwater to 1897.

events.title: Coldwater develops as a stage stop and trading point
events.summary: Billy Moore operated businesses associated with the Coldwater settlement, including a stage stop, saloon and general store serving travelers through the region.

events.title: A post office is established near Avondale Ranch
events.summary: City historical material says a post office was established near Avondale Ranch in 1896, introducing the Avondale name into the area's developing postal and settlement history.

events.title: Billy Moore serves as Coldwater postmaster
events.summary: City historical material identifies Billy Moore as Coldwater's postmaster from 1901 through 1905.

events.title: Avondale's later town site takes shape
events.summary: City historical planning material says the town site moved twice before settling in 1911 with a new post office and the Avondale name.

events.title: Goodyear Farms Historic Cemetery dates to the agricultural era
events.summary: City historical-preservation material dates Goodyear Farms Historic Cemetery to 1918. The cemetery preserves connections to migrant farm workers, agricultural families, veterans and later generations of the West Valley community.

events.title: Agua Fria River railroad bridge is built
events.summary: City historical material identifies construction of an Agua Fria River railroad bridge in 1925 as part of Avondale's transportation history.

events.title: Avondale Elementary School is established
events.summary: City historical material identifies 1937 as an important milestone in the development of local public education.

events.title: New Deal-era road improvements reach Avondale
events.summary: City historical material identifies road improvements beginning in 1938 during the New Deal era.

events.title: Agricultural migration reshapes the community
events.summary: Historical material describes migrant agricultural workers arriving in the Avondale area from Dust Bowl regions, colder Midwestern areas and other communities. Farm labor and the families who performed it became an important part of Avondale's social and economic history.

events.title: Agua Fria FSA Migratory Labor Camp opens
events.summary: The Farm Security Administration established the Agua Fria Migratory Labor Camp near Dysart Road and Van Buren Street in 1940 to provide housing and services for migrant families seeking agricultural work during the Depression era.

events.title: Riley's Bar fire exposes the need for organized fire protection
events.summary: A major fire at Riley's Bar occurred before Avondale had a formal fire department. Residents fought the blaze, and City fire-department history connects the episode with recognition of the need for incorporation and organized municipal services.

events.title: Avondale incorporates
events.summary: Avondale formally incorporated on December 16, 1946, establishing municipal government for a community that had developed from the earlier Coldwater and Avondale settlements.

events.title: Municipal police and fire services take shape
events.summary: Following incorporation, Avondale established municipal public-safety services. The early fire department operated with volunteers, with John Mabis identified by City history as its first fire chief.

events.title: Avondale population reaches 2,505
events.summary: Historical population data records 2,505 residents in Avondale in 1950.

events.title: Billy Moore Days begins
events.summary: The community celebration known as Billy Moore Days began in 1954 and became a recurring tradition connecting modern Avondale with stories about the Coldwater settlement and Billy Moore.

events.title: Regional high-school education expands
events.summary: The establishment of the Agua Fria Union High School District and Agua Fria High School became an important postwar educational milestone for Avondale and surrounding communities.

events.title: Population grows to 6,151
events.summary: Avondale's recorded population reached 6,151 by 1960, more than doubling its 1950 population.

events.title: Phoenix International Raceway opens
events.summary: Construction of Phoenix Raceway was completed in January 1964, and the Avondale facility held its first race the following month. The track became one of the city's most nationally recognizable landmarks.

events.title: Population reaches 6,626
events.summary: Historical population data records 6,626 Avondale residents in 1970.

events.title: Population reaches 8,168
events.summary: Historical population data records 8,168 Avondale residents in 1980.

events.title: NASCAR's premier series begins racing at Phoenix Raceway
events.summary: Phoenix Raceway hosted its first NASCAR Cup Series race on November 6, 1988. Alan Kulwicki won the inaugural Cup event.

events.title: Population reaches 16,169
events.summary: Avondale's population reached 16,169 by 1990 as the city entered a period of much faster growth.

events.title: Population reaches 35,883
events.summary: Avondale's population reached 35,883 in 2000, more than twice its 1990 population.

events.title: Monument Hill is listed on the National Register
events.summary: The Initial Point of the Gila and Salt River Base Line and Meridian at Monument Hill was added to the National Register of Historic Places.

events.title: Population reaches 76,238
events.summary: Avondale's population reached 76,238 in 2010, illustrating the scale of the city's late-20th and early-21st-century growth.

events.title: Oral history preserves decades of Avondale civic experience
events.summary: An oral-history interview with Marie López Rogers preserves firsthand recollections touching on Avondale community life, government, race and ethnicity, women and civic change over several decades.

events.title: 2020 Census counts 89,334 residents
events.summary: The 2020 Census counted 89,334 residents in Avondale.

events.title: Avondale surpasses 100,000 residents
events.summary: The U.S. Census Bureau estimates Avondale's population at 100,983 as of July 1, 2025, compared with 89,334 residents counted in the 2020 Census. The 2025 figure is a population estimate, not a census count.

events.title: Avondale marks 80 years since incorporation
events.summary: Avondale marked its 80th anniversary in 2026, eight decades after incorporation in December 1946.
